---
title: "system & model monitoring"
---

## monitor several layers

- monitoring collects measurements over time to identify failures or changes that need investigation
- a window is the interval being summarised, such as the last hour; a cohort is a selected group of observations

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| layer | what it describes | useful signals |
|---|---|---|
| system | whether the service operates as intended | latency, errors, request volume, resource use |
| data | whether inputs meet expectations | schema failures, missingness, freshness, distribution changes |
| predictions | what the model outputs | score distributions, predicted class proportions, model ids |
| outcomes | how predictions compare with observed targets | classification or regression metrics on labelled cohorts |

:::

- input and prediction changes are observable before labels arrive; measuring model quality requires suitable observed outcomes [data monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html), [model monitoring](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-model-quality.html)

## tools and definitions

- prometheus collects numeric time series, measurements associated with timestamps and tags; use it for service metrics and alert rules [prometheus overview](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/)
- grafana queries data sources and presents dashboards and alerts; use it to inspect trends across service and model metrics [grafana introduction](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/introduction/)
- instrumentation adds measurements to code; scraping means periodically retrieving exposed metrics
- a counter accumulates events, such as request counts, while a histogram records counts across configured value ranges, useful for latency distributions
- a dashboard displays measurements; an alert signals a condition requiring action, with an owner and response procedure

## a small instrumentation example

- the [monitoring exercise](../../examples/monitoring-demo.zip) includes `instrumentation.py`, using the prometheus python client

```python
registry = CollectorRegistry()
requests = Counter("prediction_requests_total", "prediction requests",
                   ["status_class"], registry=registry)
latency = Histogram("prediction_latency_seconds", "prediction latency", registry=registry)
requests.labels(status_class="2xx").inc()
latency.observe(0.03)
```

- `CollectorRegistry` groups metrics; `inc` adds an event and `observe` records a measurement [counters](https://prometheus.github.io/client_python/instrumenting/counter/), [histograms](https://prometheus.github.io/client_python/instrumenting/histogram/)
- this records one illustrative request; a real service updates metrics in the request path and exposes them for scraping
- monitoring labels are tags such as status class; ground-truth labels are observed prediction targets
- keep metric tags low in cardinality, meaning few distinct values; request ids create too many time series and belong in appropriately controlled logs instead [instrumentation guidance](https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/instrumentation/)

## inspect a synthetic window

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.in
python demo.py --output monitoring-output
```

- the download generates synthetic logs, features, scores, and delayed labels without requiring a deployed service
- `report.json` contains request counts, server/client error fractions, and p95 across all logged requests, including errors
- log aggregation uses pandas, a tabular-data library; numpy supplies numeric operations used by the exercise
- define denominators, latency populations, minimum sample sizes, and observation windows before setting alerts
- a runbook is a short response procedure; link it to an alert so the owner knows what to inspect and when to escalate
